abstract: Maintains offshore weather down-time estimations and operational contingency buffer margins
system_message:
You are Metocean weather analyst (MET). The Metocean weather analyst (MET) maintains offshore weather down-time estimations and operational contingency buffer margins across cable installation operations.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains offshore weather down-time estimations and operational contingency buffer margins（WTHR）
information_points.content:
MET-WTHR-U50：For Nordic Trenching and Dynamic Cable Joint Venture, the offshore weather risk mitigation schedule specifies a weather contingency buffer rate of 60 m/h based on the seasonal swell and wave window forecast to offset sea-state waiting-on-weather periods.
MET-WTHR-Z92：For Celtic Subsea Power and Marine Engineering Alliance, the offshore weather risk mitigation schedule establishes a weather contingency buffer rate of 100 m/h under the seasonal swell and wave window forecast to adjust for sea-state waiting-on-weather periods.
MET-WTHR-W1I：For Oceanic Seabed Solutions and Power Interconnect Group, the offshore weather risk mitigation schedule determines a weather contingency buffer rate of 80 m/h from the seasonal swell and wave window forecast to cover sea-state waiting-on-weather periods.

information_points.title: Significant wave height forecast（SWELL）
information_points.content:
MET-SWELL-6WU：For Oceanic Seabed Solutions and Power Interconnect Group, the hindcast metocean statistical model records a ten-year return period wave height of 3.2 m within the cable landfall approach sector.
MET-SWELL-B9X：For Celtic Subsea Power and Marine Engineering Alliance, the hindcast metocean statistical model shows a ten-year return period wave height of 5.0 m across the cable landfall approach sector.
MET-SWELL-KTC：For Nordic Trenching and Dynamic Cable Joint Venture, the hindcast metocean statistical model indicates a ten-year return period wave height of 4.1 m in the cable landfall approach sector.
